svg.title: Dispenser module wiring diagram
svg.text: Third ESP32 board: Cytron MD13S + Pololu 4752 gearmotor. Pin numbers are the ones in include/machine_settings.h.
Companion to docs/dispenser_module_hardware.md — that file has the parts list, the shops and the reasoning behind each choice.

g.text: flags with the same name are one wire (+12 V, +5 V, GND)

svg.text: 1 · POWER IN — the ISOBUS socket’s power pins, fused at the plug
PWR_GND is the return — never the seeder frame
No series diode — the ISOBUS plug is keyed.
the encoder and the shifter HV.
① Both MD13S terminal blocks ship loose —
solder them on, then wire by the silkscreen
+ − MA MB. Never by terminal-block colour:
the manual and the shop listing disagree.
② The two on-board test buttons drive the
motor whatever the ESP32 is doing. Never
press them with the auger fitted.
③ PWM low → both outputs low → stopped,
whatever DIR does. So the PWM pull-down
is the safety part; the DIR one only makes
④ Single-point ground: every GND symbol here is
one point — the − block beside the MD13S.
The return is PWR_GND, never the seeder
⑤ A resistor divider cannot replace the
BSS138: the encoder’s own pull-ups leave
its high level near 2.5 V. HV3/HV4 and
LV3/LV4 unused; one GND wire is enough.
every pin in grey is unused —
The 5V pin: with USB plugged in,
One power source at a time.
see the notes panel, top left
Grove input: 1 GND · 2 PWM · 3 DIR · 4 NC
fit them on the MD13S itself — panel 6
channel A → GPIO32 — the control loop’s speed feedback
channel B → GPIO33 — used only by the bench image, for direction
Encoder Vcc (blue) is 5 V. 12 V there puts 12 V on a GPIO and destroys the ESP32.
Cut the red and black leads out of the 1×6 header — 5.5 A stall is far too much for 0.1″ pins. Ferrules straight into the MD13S terminal block.
6 · WHAT GETS SOLDERED ONTO THE MD13S — the two 10 kΩ pull-downs and C1
On the driver beats the ESP32 end: the resistors then also hold the motor
off if the Grove cable breaks or shakes loose.
Resistors: 0805 SMD flat across the pads, or through-hole with short sleeved leads.
C1: across the POWER pads, stripe to −, body glued down — on its own legs they snap.
Find GND with a meter first: continuity from that pad to the − power terminal.
Before the first 12 V — in this order
1. Encoder BLUE goes to 5 V, never 12 V. This is the one mistake that destroys the ESP32.
2. Both 10 kΩ pull-downs fitted: unpowered, a meter reads about 10 kΩ from PWM to GND and from DIR to GND.
3. Continuity from the ESP32’s GND to the MD13S GND — and none from that ground to the seeder frame.
4. Diode-test the TVS: band to +12 V (reversed, it is a dead short). C1’s stripe goes to −.
5. One power source only. USB plugged in ⇒ take the regulator’s 5 V off the 5V pin; the grounds stay joined.
6. Meter the shifter’s LV1 / LV2 before they go anywhere near GPIO 32 / 33.
7. Coupling off the auger for every first test.
8. Once, on the tractor: key out, meter ISOBUS PWR to PWR_GND. Still live ⇒ unplug the seeder when parked for weeks.
The dispenser writes PWM 0 as the first statement in setup(). The pull-downs cover the milliseconds before that, while the ESP32 is still in reset.
